logicalBugs.explanation: Twenty’s Kanban board view arranges record cards in columns, often grouped by status or a linked record. Moving a Task or Opportunity (sales deal) card between columns saves its new status or stage but changes the destination column to manual-position ordering. The selected sort, such as Title or Amount, still appears active while cards no longer follow it; reloading the board restores the displayed order.

rootCause.explanation: A sorted cross-column board move updates the grouping field without a new position. Both the optimistic destination insertion and the subsequent reposition path order by position rather than the active record sorts, leaving moved cards out of their displayed sort order until refetch.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Twenty’s Kanban board view arranges record cards in columns, often grouped by status or a linked record. Changing an opportunity’s Kanban stage replaces the destination column’s active sort with manual-position ordering until the board is reloaded.

sourceBugs.name: Moving an opportunity between Kanban columns breaks its active sort

reproductionPaths.expected: After moving an opportunity between columns, the destination column continues to follow the selected sort.
reproductionPaths.actual: A board sorted by Close date or Name becomes incorrectly ordered after a stage change, while the selected sort indicator remains active. Keyboard column moves and side-panel Stage edits reproduce the problem. Reloading restores the correct order; no saved-sort corruption or record loss was observed.
reproSteps: Sign in to the seeded Apple workspace and create a uniquely named Opportunities Kanban view grouped by Stage.
Create three uniquely named disposable opportunities with distinct Close dates in one stage. Apply and save Close date ascending, then reload to confirm the correct sorted order.
Move one opportunity into another column using keyboard pickup and column navigation, then move it back to the original populated column.
Observe that the destination column is no longer ordered by Close date even though its ascending sort indicator remains active.
Reload the board and confirm that the correct order returns.
Repeat by changing an opportunity’s Stage through its side panel to observe the same destination-column sort loss.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Twenty’s Kanban board view arranges record cards in columns, often grouped by status or a linked record. A cross-column Task drag changes Status correctly but reorders the destination using manual position, contradicting the still-active saved Title sort.

sourceBugs.name: Dragging a Task across Kanban columns ignores its active Title sort until reload

reproductionPaths.expected: An allowed cross-column move on a sorted board should change Status while keeping the destination in the active sort order.
reproductionPaths.actual: After dragging a Task into To do on a Title-descending board, the destination settles into manual-position order while the Title sort chip and filter remain. Reload restores Title-descending order and retains the new Status. The saved sort is not deleted.
reproSteps: Create three fresh Tasks with distinct Alpha, Beta and Gamma titles; put Alpha and Gamma in To do and Beta in No Value.
Open a Status-grouped Kanban, filter to those Tasks and save Title descending. Reload and confirm Gamma precedes Alpha.
Drag Beta across columns into To do without confirming removal of sorting.
Wait for the update to settle. Observe a destination order inconsistent with descending Title while its sort chip remains.
Reload: Gamma, Beta, Alpha is restored and Beta remains To do. Repeat with a fresh setup.
Controls: an unsorted board retains its consistent manual order; same-column dragging on a sorted board offers Remove sorting, and Cancel preserves sorting.

logicalBugs.explanation: Twenty can narrow a record list with field filters and a Search any field query. Search inside a linked-record filter can find a person by either part of their name but not their full displayed name. This affects Opportunity (sales deal) Point of Contact and Company Account Owner selection; the matching person exists and individual-name searches find them.

rootCause.explanation: The relation-filter picker uses useRecordsForSelect, which searches the entire query independently in name.firstName and name.lastName. A full displayed name cannot match either component by itself.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Twenty can narrow a record list with field filters and a Search any field query. Point of Contact filter search fails for an existing contact’s full displayed name, while either individual name part finds the same contact.

sourceBugs.name: Point of Contact filter cannot find Kimberly Gordon, who is displayed on a matching opportunity

reproductionPaths.expected: The Point of Contact filter picker finds a contact using the full name displayed on the opportunity, allowing that contact to be selected.
reproductionPaths.actual: Searching the full name Kimberly Gordon returns No results even though the contact exists and is displayed on an opportunity. Searching Kimberly or Gordon finds her, and the relation edit picker also accepts the full name. The same failure reproduces with fresh contacts.
reproSteps: Sign in to the seeded Apple workspace, open Opportunities, and create a uniquely named disposable Table view.
Locate an opportunity displaying a contact with both first and last names, such as Kimberly Gordon.
Add a Point of Contact filter and enter the contact’s full displayed name in its picker search.
Observe No results, then search just the first name or last name and confirm that the same contact appears and can be selected.
Open the contact relation editor on the opportunity and verify that searching the full name finds the contact there.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Twenty can narrow a record list with field filters and a Search any field query. The Companies Account Owner filter finds a workspace member by either name part but returns No results for the same member’s full displayed name.

sourceBugs.name: Account Owner filter cannot find an existing member by their full displayed name

reproductionPaths.expected: The Account Owner filter should find an available workspace member by the full name it displays, consistent with the Account Owner cell editor.
reproductionPaths.actual: Searching Phil Schiler returns No results, while Phil or Schiler returns a selectable Phil Schiler and applies the owner filter. The Account Owner cell editor finds the full name. Both judges reproduced the failure in two fresh views; Codex also reproduced as a workspace member.
reproSteps: Sign in to the seeded workspace and create a fresh Companies Table view.
Open Filter > Account Owner and search the full displayed name of an existing owner with both first and last names, such as Phil Schiler.
Observe No results, then search the first name or surname alone and confirm the same owner appears and can be selected.
Open an Account Owner cell’s relation editor and search the same full name. Observe that the owner is found there.
Repeat in a second fresh Companies view to confirm the filter-specific failure.

logicalBugs.explanation: Twenty saved views display records in a chosen layout and retain their configured settings. Removing a saved sort and adding the same field back makes Update view fail. The replacement sort does not save, while other changes can partially persist.

rootCause.explanation: The Sort menu replaces the saved sort ID with a fresh client ID. useSaveRecordSortsToViewSorts classifies it as a create plus destroy and performs creation first; the existing saved field sort still occupies its unique key, so the create fails before deletion.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Twenty saved views display records in a chosen layout and retain their configured settings. Removing a saved sort and adding the same field back makes Update view fail. The replacement sort does not save, while other changes can partially persist.

sourceBugs.name: Readding a saved sort makes Update view fail with Migration execution failed

reproductionPaths.expected: Update view saves a valid replacement sort, including a changed direction, without an error.
reproductionPaths.actual: Update view displays Migration execution failed after a saved sort is removed and the same field is added again. The replacement fails to save and the old sort can remain after reload. Other sorts added in the same update can persist despite the error. Multiple sorts are not required to trigger the failure.
reproSteps: Sign in to the seeded Apple workspace and create a uniquely named Companies Table view.
Add a Name ascending sort and save it with Update view.
Remove the saved Name sort, then add Name again before saving. Choose descending to make the replacement distinguishable. Optionally add an Account Owner sort as well.
Click Update view and observe the Migration execution failed error.
Reload and observe that the replacement Name sort was not saved; another added sort can have persisted.
As a control, change the direction on the existing saved sort without removing and readding it, then confirm that Update view succeeds.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Twenty saved views display records in a chosen layout and retain their configured settings. Keep an existing saved sort chip, reopen Sort and choose that same field again. Update view fails with a migration error and the replacement sort does not persist; changing direction through the existing chip works.

sourceBugs.name: Reselecting a saved sort from the Sort menu creates a duplicate and fails Update view

reproductionPaths.expected: Reselecting an existing sort field should preserve or update its saved identity so Update view can persist the requested direction.
reproductionPaths.actual: After saving Title ascending and reloading, choosing Title again through Sort without removing the chip makes same-direction and descending saves fail. Retrying fails, and reload retains the original ascending sort.
reproSteps: Create a fresh Tasks Table view, add Title ascending sorting, save and reload.
Keep the existing Title sort chip. Open Sort and select Title again without removing it.
Choose descending and click Update view. Observe the migration error.
Retry and reload; the original ascending sort remains. Same-direction reselect can also fail.
Controls: initial sort creation succeeds, and toggling direction through the existing chip updates its original ID and saves correctly.

matchingGuidance.distinction: The existing reference removes and re-adds a saved sort chip. This entry retains the chip throughout and reselects its field through the Sort menu, producing the related replacement-ID/create conflict.

limitations: No task-data loss, crash or partial persistence of unrelated changes was established.
Other roles, objects and layouts are source-inferred only.

logicalBugs.explanation: Twenty’s Calendar view places records on dates using a chosen date field. Switching a grouped Table or board to Calendar can leave the calendar configured with one date field while its records use another. Records may disappear despite existing in the displayed period, or Task cards may use a different date from the Due Date shown in the selector. This concerns layout transitions rather than changing a record’s saved date.

rootCause.explanation: Calendar entry first loads new date/calendar state, then updateCurrentView handles the grouping reset by calling loadRecordIndexStates with its captured pre-update currentView. That second full-state load restores old calendar metadata and grouping, so the calendar query has an invalid/stale configuration until reload.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Twenty’s Calendar view places records on dates using a chosen date field. Changing a grouped Table or Kanban (a board of cards in columns) view to Calendar produces a blank calendar even though Creation date is selected and records exist in the displayed month.

sourceBugs.name: Switching a grouped view to Calendar hides all events until reload

reproductionPaths.expected: Switching to Calendar displays records on the selected Creation date, including records previously visible in the grouped view, without requiring a reload or date-field reselection.
reproductionPaths.actual: Calendar displays no events or overflow links after the layout switch, while the menu still shows Creation date. Reloading the same view or selecting Creation date again restores events. Ungrouped Table-to-Calendar switching works. The failure reproduces for People grouped by Company and Companies grouped by Account Owner.
reproSteps: Sign in to the seeded Apple workspace and create a uniquely named People Table view containing records created in the month you will inspect.
Group the view by Company. Records without a company remain visible under No Value; adding relation groups is unnecessary.
Switch through Kanban, then choose Options > Layout > Calendar. A direct grouped Table-to-Calendar switch can also reproduce the failure.

Confirm Date field is Creation date, End date field is None, and the displayed month includes the records' creation dates. Observe that Calendar contains no events, including for people visible in No Value before the switch.
Reload the same view without changing its settings and observe that events appear. Selecting Creation date again also restores them.
As a control, switch a fresh ungrouped Table view directly to Calendar and confirm that its dated records appear.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Twenty’s Calendar view places records on dates using a chosen date field. Start with a saved Tasks Calendar using Due Date, switch through Kanban (a board of cards in columns) and return to Calendar. The selector still shows Due Date while cards are placed using a different date field.

sourceBugs.name: Calendar Date field checks Creation date while cards still use Due Date

reproductionPaths.actual: After Calendar→Kanban→Calendar, the saved view and Date field menu select Creation date, but the existing cards remain on their Due Date days. A fresh Table-only round trip keeps the menu and placement consistent; reload makes the affected calendar follow the saved field.
reproSteps: Create own Tasks whose Due Dates differ clearly from their Creation dates. Create a fresh Tasks Calendar using Due Date and verify matching placement/checkmark.
Switch through a Kanban layout grouped by Status, then return to Calendar without reloading.
Open Options → Date field and compare the checked Creation date with cards still placed on Due Dates. Repeat on another fresh view.
Compare a fresh Calendar→Table→Calendar round trip and a full reload of the affected view.

logicalBugs.explanation: Twenty can narrow a record list with field filters and a Search any field query. Changing which field an already-saved filter uses does not reliably replace the old field. New values can be saved under the previous field, producing incorrect labels or empty results after reload, or a valid rule for the new type can fail validation against the old field.

rootCause.explanation: The existing view-filter update payload includes value, operand and target/subfield changes but omits fieldMetadataId. Changing the source field is detected as an edit yet persists the new values against the old field.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Twenty can narrow a record list with field filters and a Search any field query. Changing an existing saved filter from Amount to Stage saves the Stage values but retains the old Amount field. Reloading displays raw Stage values under Amount and returns no matching records.

sourceBugs.name: Changing a saved advanced-filter field persists new values under the old field

reproductionPaths.expected: Update view should persist the changed field together with its operator and values, so reload restores the same Stage filter and matching rows shown in the preview.
reproductionPaths.actual: The Stage preview returns matching rows, but after a completed Update view and reload the rule reads Amount Is not ["PROPOSAL","CUSTOMER"] and returns zero rows. The field-save failure and raw-value display are symptoms of the same omitted field change.
reproSteps: Sign in and create a fresh Opportunities Table view.
Add an advanced Amount Is not 450000 rule, save the view, and wait for saving to complete.
Edit that existing rule by changing its field to Stage, choosing Is not, and selecting Proposal and Customer.
Confirm the preview contains matching opportunities.
Close the filter editor, click Update view, and wait for saving to finish.
Reload and reopen the advanced rule. Observe Amount Is not ["PROPOSAL","CUSTOMER"] rather than Stage Is not Proposal, Customer, with zero matching rows.
As a control, remove the corrupted rule and create a new Stage Is not Proposal, Customer rule; save and reload to observe that this newly created rule persists correctly.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Twenty can narrow a record list with field filters and a Search any field query. Change the field used by an existing saved advanced-filter rule to a field of another type, then save. Validation still treats the rule as belonging to the old field, so the newly valid condition is rejected.

sourceBugs.name: Changing a saved Name filter to a relative date rule fails because its old field is retained

reproductionPaths.expected: Saving a changed advanced-filter field should persist that field together with its valid operator and value.
reproductionPaths.actual: Changing a saved Name rule to Creation date Is relative This day sends the new operand/value without the new field ID. The server rejects the date operator against the retained Name field with “Filter operand is not supported for this field type.” Reload restores the original rule.
reproSteps: Create a fresh People view, add an advanced Name filter and save the view.
Edit that saved rule by changing its field to Creation date and choosing Is relative → This day.
Save the updated view and observe the unsupported-operand error.
Reload and observe that the original Name filter remains saved.
Control: create a new Creation date Is relative This day rule directly; save and reload to confirm it persists.

logicalBugs.explanation: Twenty can divide table rows or board cards into groups based on a field value. Record-list header counts and grouped Table calculations can disagree with the rows that are displayed. Combining search, field filters or group conditions can leave summaries counting excluded records; in a Workflow Runs (execution history) table, linked-record grouping can instead show matching rows with a zero total. These cases concern incorrect summaries, not missing saved records.

rootCause.explanation: Table footer and header aggregate hooks combine independently compiled filters using object spread. Group, explicit filters and any-field search can each contain top-level and/or keys; later objects replace earlier predicates rather than conjoining them, so summaries include records excluded by the row query.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Twenty can divide table rows or board cards into groups based on a field value. Filtering a Stage-grouped Opportunities (sales deals) table to one stage removes the other stages’ rows, but their empty groups still show Amount averages and other calculations from excluded records.

sourceBugs.name: Grouped table calculations include records excluded by the active filter

reproductionPaths.expected: Each group calculation should respect both the active view filter and the group condition. Groups with no matching records should not display values calculated from excluded records.
reproductionPaths.actual: With Stage Is Meeting applied, only Meeting rows remain, while empty New and Screening groups still show Amount averages such as 547k and 546.3k. The incorrect calculations persist after saving and reloading; Sum and Earliest Close date also include excluded records.
reproSteps: Sign in and create a fresh Opportunities Table view.
Group the table by Stage and leave empty groups visible.
Set the Amount group-footer calculation to Average.
Apply the single filter Stage Is Meeting.
Observe that only Meeting contains rows, but empty New, Screening and other excluded groups still display nonzero Amount averages.
Save the view, wait for saving to complete, and reload. Observe that the incorrect group calculations persist.
As controls, use an ungrouped table or add an additional nonrestrictive Name or Amount filter alongside Stage; these calculations respect the active filters.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Twenty can divide table rows or board cards into groups based on a field value. Combining Search any field with advanced OR rules displays the correct matching records but reports a larger total that ignores the advanced rules.

sourceBugs.name: Search combined with advanced OR filters reports an incorrect total count

reproductionPaths.expected: The total count should use the same combined search and advanced-filter conditions as the displayed records. Six matching opportunities should produce a count of six.
reproductionPaths.actual: Search any field Corporate combined with Name Contains iPhone OR Name Contains Apple Store displays six matching cards but reports 12. The mismatch persists after a completed save and reload, repeats in Table, and can report a nonzero count for an empty result set.
reproSteps: Sign in and create a fresh Opportunities Kanban view grouped by Stage.
Apply Search any field with Corporate and observe 12 matches in the seeded data.
Add advanced rules Name Contains iPhone and Name Contains Apple Store, joined with OR.
Observe three iPhone Corporate Program cards and three Apple Store Corporate Training cards, while the view total remains 12.
Dismiss the filter editor, click Update view, and wait until Update view disappears before reloading.
Observe that the saved view still contains six matching cards but reports 12; no additional cards or Load more controls account for the difference.
Switch the same saved filters to Table and observe the same total-count mismatch.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Twenty can divide table rows or board cards into groups based on a field value. A single basic People Name filter combined with Search any field filters the visible rows correctly but leaves the total count and footer calculations describing the larger search-only result set.

sourceBugs.name: People summaries ignore a basic Name filter combined with Search any field

reproductionPaths.expected: The view total and column calculations should describe the same records as the filtered table rows.
reproductionPaths.actual: With a unique Name filter plus Designer search, one matching person with no email is shown while the header reports the larger search-only count and Unique of Emails reports 43 instead of zero. Empty-of-Phones percentages and earliest creation dates also include excluded people. Both judges reproduced the mismatch and confirmed that it persists after a completed save and reload.
reproSteps: Create a fresh People Table view and three disposable people sharing a unique name prefix. Give one Job Title Designer, leave that person’s email empty, and give the other two Job Title Engineer with distinct known email values.
Apply a single basic Name Contains filter for the unique prefix. Set the Emails footer to Unique and verify the rows, count and calculation agree for the three people.

Add Search any field with Designer while retaining that single Name filter. Observe only the Designer person remains, but the header count and email calculation describe the larger search-only set rather than the visible person.
Save the view, wait for saving to complete, and reload. Observe that the mismatched total and calculations persist.

As controls, remove Search any field and verify the three-person summaries return. Replace the Name filter with Job Title Contains Engineer and search the unique prefix; observe that rows and summaries agree.
Optionally inspect Empty of Phones or Earliest of Creation date to see that additional calculations include excluded records under the failing Name-plus-search condition.

logicalBugs.explanation: Twenty saved views display records in a chosen layout and retain their configured settings. Shift-clicking a table row range leaves the clicked endpoint visibly checked but excludes it from the selected count and bulk-action targets.

rootCause.explanation: Row checkbox clicks are handled by the wrapping div while the inner Checkbox maintains its own checked state. Shift range selection toggles the current row from shared selection state while the inner primitive also handles the click; their separate updates can leave the endpoint visibly checked without its row-selection atom participating in the bulk selection.
rootCause.assessment: Source-informed hypothesis: the cited implementation contains the relevant failure boundary, but the exact triggering event order was not independently reproduced during this clustering pass.

logicalBugs.explanation: Twenty’s Company Domain Name field stores a URL and an optional display label. A negative filter such as Doesn’t contain .com wrongly excludes a non-.com domain when its optional label is empty, even though that URL satisfies the filter. A populated label can avoid the exclusion; positive Contains filtering works.

rootCause.explanation: The LINKS Does not contain converter combines negative ILIKE checks across composite link fields without admitting null primary labels. SQL NOT of a comparison with NULL remains unknown, so a company with an unset label is excluded even when its URL does not contain the query.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Twenty’s Company Domain Name field stores a URL and an optional display label. A populated label can avoid the exclusion; positive Contains filtering works.

sourceBugs.name: Domain Name Doesn’t contain excludes companies with an unset link label

reproductionPaths.expected: Domain Name Doesn’t contain .com includes a populated .org or other non-.com URL even when the URL has no optional link label.
reproductionPaths.actual: Contains .com correctly selects the .com company, but switching to Doesn’t contain excludes the unlabeled .org company and can leave an isolated pair with no results. Seeded Google with domain goo.gle is also wrongly excluded. A nonmatching URL with a populated link label can remain visible, so exclusion is conditional rather than universal.
reproSteps: Sign in to the seeded Apple workspace and open Companies. Create two uniquely named disposable companies, one with a .org Domain Name URL and one with a .com URL. Leave their optional link labels unset.
Filter Name to the unique prefix so both test companies are visible.
Add Domain Name Contains .com and confirm that only the .com company remains.
Change that filter to Doesn’t contain .com. Observe that no test companies appear, although the .org company should match.
Reset the Domain Name filter and confirm that both companies return. Repeat the positive/negative sequence to confirm the result.
As a seeded-data comparison, verify that Google with domain goo.gle is visible unfiltered but omitted under Domain Name Doesn’t contain .com.

logicalBugs.explanation: Twenty can narrow a record list with field filters and a Search any field query. Record-page Next/Previous omits the originating list’s Search any field query and navigates to records outside the matching results.

rootCause.explanation: useQueryVariablesFromParentView reconstructs navigation filters from parentViewFilters and parentViewFilterGroups but does not include the separate anyFieldFilterValue. Neighbor and count queries therefore navigate the full saved/explicit-filter view rather than the searched subset.

rootCause.explanation: turnAnyFieldFilterIntoRecordGqlFilter handles selected scalar/composite metadata types but has no RICH_TEXT branch. Task/Note bodyV2 BlockNote content consequently contributes no predicate to Search any field.

rootCause.explanation: View sort persistence stores field/direction/subfield but no priority position; loading maps viewSorts in returned metadata order without restoring the active sort sequence. Multiple sort precedence can therefore change after metadata reload.

logicalBugs.explanation: Twenty’s Kanban board view arranges record cards in columns, often grouped by status or a linked record. Moving an opportunity in an Amount-filtered Kanban can throw an amountMicros error before saving when the record was previously loaded without its Amount field. The card appears to move, but totals stay stale and reload restores its old stage.

rootCause.explanation: Optimistic list-filter evaluation passes record[filterKey] into isMatchingCurrencyFilter without ensuring a currency value was fetched. A partially cached Opportunity lacks Amount, and the matcher dereferences amountMicros before the stage mutation can complete.

rootCause.explanation: The client can initialize active sorts once from stale cached view metadata. Later fresh saved sorts do not reinitialize that active list, and Update view interprets missing active sorts as intentional deletions.

logicalBugs.explanation: Twenty can narrow a record list with field filters and a Search any field query. Ordinary UI Contains and Does not contain filters interpret typed percent and underscore as SQL wildcard syntax, including records without the typed punctuation or excluding them incorrectly.

rootCause.explanation: The shared UI filter converter interpolates raw text into percent-wrapped ILIKE patterns, including composite-name tokens, without escaping user-entered percent or underscore. The server correctly evaluates those supplied patterns.

Enter a literal percent sign or underscore in a Contains or Does not contain text filter. reproSteps: Create fresh People with a unique common name prefix, for example QA Alpha and QA Beta, with neither name containing a percent sign.

Compare a record actually containing a percent sign and ordinary-text filters. Repeat on fresh data; saving and reloading the filtered view retains the pattern behavior.
For underscore, compare names differing by one character and apply a Contains value with an underscore in that position; observe the underscore acts as a wildcard rather than requiring the character.

limitations: No explicit maintainer ruling on literal versus wildcard punctuation in UI Contains was located; the accepted literal-text contract remains an inference supported by docs and the matching proposal.
The clearer current documentation postdates the 2026-07-30 fixture source; the matching pre-pin PR was not merged.

logicalBugs.explanation: Twenty’s Kanban board view arranges record cards in columns, often grouped by status or a linked record. Changing grouping or layout on a built-in saved view can revert its effective grouping and leave a blank Table, Kanban (a board of cards in columns) or Calendar despite a nonzero record count. rootCause.explanation: MetadataEventPublisher routes view events through the generic overridable-entity sanitizer, but resolveOverridableEntityEventBatchOverrides does not include view in its supported entities. The event therefore pushes base built-in view properties instead of effective saved overrides. Frontend metadata then replaces the effective layout/grouping with base values while associated group configuration remains changed.
